\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{редко} (rédko)}{редко (rédko)}]{\ru{редко} (rédko) — rarely}

\label{lesson:RU-C150-redko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for dawn, then the Russian for sunset.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{редко}}
\textbf{\ru{редко}} (\emph{rédko}) — \textquotedblleft{}rarely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{редко}} is \emph{\ru{редкий}}, \textquotedblleft{}sparse, rare\textquotedblright{}, made into an adverb. Vasmer relates \emph{\ru{редкий}} to Lithuanian \emph{rẽtas}, \textquotedblleft{}sparse, rare\textquotedblright{}, and Latin \emph{rēte}, \textquotedblleft{}a net\textquotedblright{}: a net is all gaps.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rédko}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{rédko}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for dawn, then the Russian for sunset, then say \emph{rédko} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{каждый} (kázhdyy)}{каждый (kázhdyy)}]{\ru{каждый} (kázhdyy) — every, each}

\label{lesson:RU-C150-kazhdyy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for sunset, then the Russian for rarely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{каждый}}
\textbf{\ru{каждый}} (\emph{kázhdyy}) — \textquotedblleft{}every, each\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{каждый}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*kŭžĭdo} — inherited: the old question stem of \emph{\ru{кто}}, \textquotedblleft{}who\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{\ru{же}}, a stressing particle, and \emph{-\ru{де}}, as in \emph{\ru{где}}, \textquotedblleft{}where\textquotedblright{} (Vasmer). Gothic \emph{hvarjis}, \textquotedblleft{}which\textquotedblright{}, is built in a similar way.
\end{cousinweb}
